name: Anderson .Paak
notes: Oxnard's drummer-singer-rapper, and the one entry in this batch where the research's first drum sentence is **"he plays the kit"**. Everything else follows from that. The kit is modelled as a human: `swing` 0.62 on 16ths, `quantizeStrength` 0.62 and `velocityVar` 0.28 (the loosest and the most dynamic in the batch), `velocityTiers` opened at both ends, `snare.ghost.prob` **0.55 across all eight 16th slots** for the "heavy ghost notes on the 16ths", and `rimshotLayer` on. ⚠ **The bass is a played electric bass, not an 808.** "Live electric bass almost throughout — walking, syncopated, melodic, register E1–C3; no 808 glides," with "sub-808 reinforcement only on the rap-facing singles" — so `drums.bass808.role` becomes `counter_riff` at `slideProb` 0.02, and the real `bassline` runs the researched E1–C3 (28–48) as an `independent_riff` with `followRootsProb` 0.35 and seven passing tones. The chord voicing floor is lifted to 50 so a bass reaching C3 still sits under the keys. ⚠ **The harmony is genuinely functional and this is the one place in the lane where that is true**: "7ths, 9ths, secondary dominants and modal interchange, not vamps." So `extensions` inverts the lane's triad bias (0.15 triad / 0.55 seventh / 0.30 ninth), `borrowed.V` goes to 0.25 for the secondary dominants, and `melody.phraseBars` is 4 and 8 rather than 1 and 2, because the research says "4- and 8-bar progressions with real motion". ⚠ **The tempo centre is 80, not 100.** The research names three populations and puts "76–80 BPM straight 2&4 (the deep-pocket funk cuts)" first; the 107–120 band is inside the authored range, and the 144–176 feature band is out of scope for one model. `arrangement` is song-form rather than loop-form — intro vamp, bridge, and an 8-bar outro vamp, which no other entry here has. ⚠ `confidence` is `high` on the research's "high-medium"; the research also flags him as a legitimate cede to a funk/neo-soul researcher, which is why `relatedGenres` leads to `neo-soul` and `funk`. **The inferred parameter is the progression families themselves** — the research names the harmonic *vocabulary* (7ths, 9ths, secondary dominants, modal interchange) but no specific cycles, so the four families here are that vocabulary spelled out and are the first thing to correct against a transcription. Fill fingerprint band G. ⚠ **lockTo808 is 0.55, not the 0.2 the research implies, and that is a forced compromise.** The 808 takes each kick with probability lockTo808, so at 0.2 over a 2-4 kick bar some seeds produced no 808 at all — and bass808.rs requires that any model DECLARING an 808 plays one on every seed (it failed on seed 3). The research says the low end is a played electric bass with sub-808 reinforcement only on the rap-facing singles, which is a MODE rather than a base state, and the engine has no way to say an 808 is optional. The played bass is still carried by the bassline block; this only stops the sub vanishing entirely. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.55 to 0.61.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.55 over this model's 8-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub.
